events.text: Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps says that it struck two tankers trying to pass the Strait of Hormuz with aerial protection from the United States, and forced four others to turn around.

At least 11 Palestinians, including four children, are injured during a raid by Israeli settlers and soldiers in Nablus in the occupied West Bank. Israeli soldiers also detain at least ten people from Nablus, Tell, Salim, and Bethlehem.
Hamas says that they will disarm if Israel withdraws from and ends its military campaign in the Gaza Strip and if Israel and the U.S. honors the ceasefire agreement signed in October 2025.
The Israel Defense Forces says that they have violated the ceasefire by killing two Hamas operatives accused of smuggling weapons into the Gaza Strip in separate strikes.
A migrant worker is killed and another is injured in a shooting attack by insurgents in Kulgam district, Jammu and Kashmir, India.
The Human Rights Watch reports that an Sukhoi Su-24 airstrike by the Russian paramilitary group Africa Corps in Mali's Mopti region killed eight civilians in June.
A bus en route to Algiers, Algeria, plunges into a deep ravine in El Kerma after skidding off the road, killing 25 people and injuring 44 others.
Two bodies and a body part are recovered after an avalanche on the Broad Peak in Pakistan buried ten climbers yesterday, including Nirmal Purja, who remains missing.
At least 34 miners are killed in a methane gas explosion at a coal mine near Quetta, Pakistan.
Ceutan mayor-president Juan Jesús Vivas says that around 60,000 undocumented migrants have entered the Spanish exclave in North Africa in the last 24 hours, as the death toll rises to 57.
Videos on social media appear to show the Spanish Army deploying military vehicles towards the border with Morocco.
French interior minister Laurent Nuñez announces that he has ordered increased controls at the border with Spain amid fears the thousands of migrants entering Ceuta could make their way to France.

Austrian chancellor Christian Stocker and Finnish interior minister Mari Rantanen join Italian prime minister Giorgia Meloni in calling for Spain to be suspended from Schengen Area in response to the mass arrival of migrants in Ceuta over t
Spanish authorities close the Melilla border crossing with Morocco after around 400 migrants stormed the border barrier. RTVE reports the sound of gunfire and explosions.

A Sri Lankan court sentences former police chief Pujith Jayasundara to death for negligence in failing to prevent the 2019 Easter bombings, which killed 279 people. Sri Lanka has not carried out an execution since 1976.
Indonesian authorities announces it arrested a Malaysia Airlines pilot for allegedly smuggling over {{cvt|26|kg|lbs}} of ecstasy and a package of methamphetamine into Jakarta International Airport.
The Bulgaria National Assembly sets October 25th as the date for the presidential election.

Carlos Cordeiro, senior FIFA executive and adviser to FIFA president Gianni Infantino, resigns in protest of Infantino's plans, calling them "a bad deal for FIFA's members, a bad deal for football, and a bad deal for the long-term future of
It is reported that CONCACAF chief Victor Montagliani is considering running against FIFA president Gianni Infantino in next year's election.
